scope: 127 future bounded tasks. Current authored API/UI, practice/account/history and gVisor implementation are retained, not reopened as missing. Stable IDs are distinct from topologically sorted execution order.
review_workflow: Other AI tools implement one ready issue per branch/PR; designated maintainer/assistant reviews actual code and observed checks before an authorized merge. No self-merge/automatic merger or unattended monitoring is enabled.

issues.title: Enforce an evidence contract for contributor pull requests
issues.problem: The requested multi-tool workflow needs PR submissions that the reviewing assistant can assess consistently. Instructions alone do not show whether a contributor mapped an issue, respected scope or actually ran a claimed check.
scope: Extend the PR evidence contract with stable backlog ID, before/after behavior, exact changed paths, dependency status, tests actually run with fail/skip/unrun states, security/data impact and rollback.
Add a narrow pull-request metadata check that reports missing sections or an unknown/missing issue reference; keep implementation review and merge authorization with the designated reviewer.
Require external AI tools to submit focused PRs and corrections rather than bypassing review; recognize explicit owner overrides for exceptional direct-main work.
Apply the evidence gate to all contributor PRs; do not infer or classify authorship as AI/human from content.
acceptance: A fixture PR with all required evidence passes the metadata check; fixtures with no issue ID or invented empty test evidence fail with an actionable explanation.
An explicit not-run explanation is allowed when the owner forbids testing; the check never forces fabricated results.
The workflow never executes arbitrary PR-body text and never grants write permission or auto-merges a PR.
validation: Inspect the proposed PR template and run the metadata-check fixtures introduced by this issue.
Inspect workflow permissions and fork-PR handling; do not run pull-request head code with write credentials.
out_of_scope: Automatically approving or merging all AI contributions
Reimplementing the repository-wide instructions the owner is already updating
issues.risk: Untrusted PR text must remain data, and evidence completeness must not be presented as substantive review.
issues.completion_evidence: Implemented scripts/github/check_pr_evidence.py and read-only trusted-base PR workflow;37 scoped evidence cases and the complete50-case tooling suite passed. Source/contract reviewed for inert data, stale heads and malformed events. Hosted workflow execution and branch-rule enforcement remain unverified and separate from metadata completeness.

issues.title: Enforce owner-approved reviewed-merge rules for the main branch
issues.problem: A written review-only workflow does not restrict credentials that can currently write main. The actual GitHub branch rules and reviewer identities must be verified before distributed contributors rely on enforced review.
scope: Have the repository owner name the actual reviewer identities and approve a narrow emergency-maintenance policy; do not invent an assistant GitHub account.
Configure supported main-branch rules requiring PR review and the verified check contexts, protecting against forced updates/deletion and documenting any unavoidable owner bypass.
Record the effective rules and hosting-plan limitations without exposing tokens; preserve access for the designated review/merge workflow.
acceptance: An authorized read of effective branch rules confirms review/check requirements and protected history.
The owner can identify which principals may merge and which emergency bypasses remain; the documentation does not claim an assistant monitors or approves work continuously.
If permissions or hosting-plan capabilities block enforcement, the issue remains explicitly blocked with the exact prerequisite rather than claiming policy prose enforced it.
validation: Read the effective GitHub rules/protection configuration using authorized API access and review the required check context names.
Use a disposable authorized repository/rule fixture for any negative push experiments; never test forced updates or destructive changes on main.
out_of_scope: Creating or sharing new credentials in chat
Changing repository visibility or purchasing a hosting plan
issues.risk: Incorrect rules can block maintainers or leave unreviewed writes possible. Owner authorization and verified actual identities are prerequisites.
issues.owner_role: Repository owner and designated security reviewer

issues.title: Record owner-approved original-code licensing and inbound contribution rights
issues.problem: The original project has no selected outbound license or settled inbound IP policy. Inviting many AI-assisted contributors without an explicit rights decision leaves reuse and contribution expectations unclear.
scope: Prepare a short decision record comparing owner-selected licensing options and how external human/AI-assisted contributions are accepted.
Obtain the actual owner decision, record its date and scope, and only then add or amend license/notice files and contributor declarations.
Distinguish original application rights from preserved upstream MIT/Apache code, datasets, problems and model artifacts.
acceptance: The owner-approved decision states exact rights for original code and the inbound contribution mechanism; undecided points remain explicitly blocked.
Contributor instructions identify third-party attribution and provenance requirements without claiming ownership of upstream or user code.
A PR containing this change includes the owner decision reference and reviewer evidence required by B001.
validation: Statically review the decision, selected license text and contributor notice for consistency.
Review the diff to ensure preserved upstream notices and archive hashes were not changed.
out_of_scope: Choosing a license without owner authority
issues.risk: An assistant cannot invent licensing consent or assign rights it does not own.

issues.title: Approve a small pilot charter and data lifecycle contract
issues.problem: The existing local app can support learning, but first audience, public-hosting responsibility, retention periods, deletion and provider-sharing consent remain unresolved. These decisions are prerequisites for handling real learner data.
scope: Document a deliberately small first pilot audience and the existing practice/account/history features included.
Have the owner specify retention and deletion rules for source, accounts, logs, exports and backups, including how in-flight jobs and legal exceptions are handled.
Record who operates the pilot, its approved resource ceiling, incident contact and whether external model sharing is disabled; keep paid services off by default.
acceptance: A decision table names each stored data class, purpose, owner, retention trigger and deletion/export behavior.
No private submission is eligible for training or external provider transfer without explicit separately recorded consent.
Pilot launch criteria distinguish local readiness, controlled pilot access and public production exposure; unapproved budget or hosting choices remain blocked.
validation: Review the charter against current source locations and the technical-debt privacy/operations gates.
Have the owner approve the decision record; no runtime or paid-service call is required.
out_of_scope: Implementing billing or an AI provider
Inventing a retention period or hosting budget without owner approval
issues.risk: Policy choices affect irreversible deletion and public trust; engineering must follow recorded owner decisions.

issues.title: Pin CI actions to immutable reviewed commits
issues.problem: CI currently references checkout, setup-node, setup-uv and upload-artifact by mutable major tags. Package locks do not pin the executable action implementations.
scope: Resolve each currently used action to an official reviewed commit and record the readable release alongside the digest.
Keep workflow permissions at the existing minimum and document a bounded update/review process.
Preserve frozen installs and existing check coverage rather than replacing the workflow.
acceptance: Every third-party uses entry is pinned to a full commit SHA from the official upstream.
No new token write permission, unsafe pull_request_target execution or secret exposure is introduced.
The workflow configuration still contains all existing required steps and explicit artifact retention.
validation: Statically inspect all uses entries, source provenance and workflow permissions.
When check execution is authorized, observe a normal fork-safe PR CI run at the exact commit and record its outcome.
out_of_scope: Running untrusted PR code with repository write credentials
issues.risk: Incorrect action provenance can install a malicious implementation; digest updates require review.

issues.title: Pin web and API container bases and align intended Python patch versions
issues.problem: The judge base is already digest-pinned, while web/API image tags remain mutable and the API Python pin is broader than the root patch pin. Rebuilding can silently select different toolchains.
scope: Select supported official web/API base-image identities and pin immutable digests while preserving their current nonroot and read-only runtime assumptions.
Reconcile the intended root and API Python patch policy with actual documented supported versions; do not silently widen dependency compatibility.
Document how digest/patch updates are reviewed and refreshed.
acceptance: Web/API base-image references include reviewed digests and readable versions.
Root/API Python pins express one intentional policy and frozen dependency installation remains enabled.
A later authorized build produces artifacts without runtime keys, databases or AnalyseFuture content; no TLS or checksum verification is disabled.
validation: Statically review Docker stages, image origins and version pins.
When builds are authorized: npm run build; docker build --secret id=proxy_ca,src=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt -t solver-ai-api:pin-check services/api.
issues.risk: Image updates may change OS libraries or runtime behavior; preserve rollback digests and verify supported architecture.

issues.title: Reject plaintext external identity and worker transport configuration
issues.problem: AUTH_JWKS_URL currently permits HTTP for any hostname. Local loopback/Compose routes need support, but the same permissive configuration can be unsafe across an untrusted network.
scope: Define an explicit local/trusted-private transport policy and reject external plaintext JWKS, issuer and worker API routes by default.
Validate origins, credentials, fragments and configured destinations once at startup with safe error messages.
Keep documented loopback and explicitly selected private Compose development routes usable without disabling TLS validation.
acceptance: Configuration fixtures accept supported local routes and HTTPS external routes, and reject a public HTTP hostname, embedded credentials and malformed origins.
A denied configuration fails startup before accepting authenticated traffic; no URL credentials appear in errors.
Existing fixed-destination, no-redirect JWKS behavior and worker credential separation remain intact.
issues.risk: A broad private-network exception would recreate the gap; explicit development exemptions need owner-reviewed scope.

issues.title: Add a total JWKS fetch deadline with real transport fixtures
issues.problem: JWKS refresh uses HTTPX operation timeouts and a size cap but has no outer elapsed-time bound. A slow stream can hold authentication refresh longer than the nominal five-second timeout; most existing tests stub the fetch function.
scope: Wrap the full JWKS transfer and decoding path in an explicit total deadline with a monotonic/async cancellation mechanism.
Add HTTPX transport fixtures for slow chunks, redirects, oversized/incorrect Content-Length, invalid JSON and cancellation.
Preserve refresh cooldown, cache locking, fixed algorithms and safe unavailable-versus-unauthorized responses.
acceptance: A slow trickle terminates at the configured total deadline rather than extending on every chunk.
Redirects and bodies above 65,536 bytes are rejected, including missing/false length headers.
Concurrent refresh requests do not create unbounded fetches and valid cached-key behavior remains covered.
out_of_scope: Changing JWT algorithms or trusting token-supplied key URLs
Live calls to arbitrary JWKS hosts in tests
issues.risk: Cancellation and cache-state changes can accidentally deny all users or accept stale keys; fixtures must exercise both failure and recovery.

issues.title: Describe protected endpoints with an accurate OpenAPI bearer scheme
issues.problem: Manual bearer parsing enforces authentication but does not expose a usable security scheme in interactive API docs. A docs-only scheme must not relax duplicate-header or strict signature checks.
scope: Declare bearer security metadata for protected learner endpoints while retaining require_user as the authorization authority.
Keep public catalog/health endpoints public and worker-only routes visibly separate from learner token authentication.
Extend schema assertions to verify correct security declarations, not merely path presence.
acceptance: OpenAPI contains one documented learner bearer scheme and protected submission/hint endpoints reference it.
Public catalog endpoints do not advertise a mandatory bearer token.
Duplicate authorization headers, wrong issuer/audience/algorithm and token-supplied URLs still fail exactly as before.
validation: uv run --project services/api --frozen pytest services/api/tests/catalog/test_api.py services/api/tests/identity/test_auth.py
out_of_scope: Adding a new API-key login mechanism
issues.risk: Convenience helpers can mask duplicate headers or bypass the existing verifier; the security dependency must remain authoritative.

issues.title: Validate production worker credential strength before enabling internal routes
issues.problem: The native runner generates a strong local worker token, but the API accepts configured worker bearer material without an independent strength check. A manually supplied weak production value can define the whole controller trust domain.
scope: Centralize worker credential validation for configured internal-route enablement, with a documented minimum entropy/length policy and no public fallback key.
Keep the existing secure local generation path and distinguish deliberately disabled judging from invalid configured credentials.
Reject invalid credentials at configuration time without logging their value.
acceptance: Empty/unset worker auth leaves execution unavailable as documented; a nonempty weak configured value fails clearly.
Generated local tokens and a valid production-format fixture enable the existing authenticated control flow.
Logs, API errors and diagnostics contain no token values or token-derived reversible representation.
out_of_scope: Printing or requesting real secret values
issues.risk: Overly broad validation could break deliberate no-judge development; disabled mode and invalid mode need distinct tests.

issues.title: Support bounded worker bearer rotation without an outage
issues.problem: The controller trust domain relies on one configured bearer, with no tested handover protocol. Replacing it can abruptly stop heartbeat/lease/completion requests during active work.
scope: Design a narrow current/previous credential handover with an explicit short overlap deadline and constant-time comparisons.
Document update order and rollback for API and existing workers; prohibit permanent previous-token acceptance.
Cover active completion during rotation and expiry without extending arbitrary job authorization.
acceptance: During the bounded overlap both approved credentials work; after expiry the previous credential receives the existing unauthorized response.
An active worker can complete only its valid lease and cannot cross worker/job ownership during rotation.
Unknown credentials and expired overlap fail closed, and token material never enters logs or public capability responses.
out_of_scope: Rotating real deployment credentials in this issue without operator authorization
issues.risk: A permissive grace window can preserve a compromised key; require operator-controlled expiry and revoke procedure.

issues.title: Introduce an explicit trusted-ingress identity throttle policy
issues.problem: Local auth deliberately uses shared per-path buckets because no trusted ingress is configured. This prevents spoofed forwarding bypasses but is not suitable as a complete public per-client abuse policy.
scope: Add a disabled-by-default trusted-proxy/header configuration tied to an explicit ingress deployment contract.
Retain the current safe shared-bucket fallback for direct local access and reject ambiguous forwarding configurations.
Exercise the same Better Auth sign-in/sign-up rules through trusted and untrusted request fixtures.
acceptance: Spoofed X-Forwarded-For from an untrusted direct caller cannot obtain a new throttle identity.
A request from the configured trusted ingress resolves only the reviewed client-address field and cannot append arbitrary hops.
Independent legitimate clients do not all share the same public deployment throttle bucket, while local safe defaults remain unchanged.
out_of_scope: Assuming any forwarding header is trustworthy
issues.risk: Trusting client-controlled IP headers weakens existing defenses; proxy provenance must be enforced, not inferred from a header name.

issues.title: Create a consistent private backup and restore procedure for both stores
issues.problem: Local SQLite databases and the web signing/session secret must be preserved together, but no tested coordinated backup/restore procedure exists. Copying live WAL files casually can produce an unusable or inconsistent recovery.
scope: Implement a trusted operator helper using supported SQLite backup/quiescence semantics for auth and submissions plus required private key material.
Write a manifest of revision/schema and checksums in a private archive outside Git, with restrictive modes and explicit destination handling.
Document restore into a fresh temporary workspace and the policy for queued/in-flight work; require confirmation before replacing real state.
acceptance: A temporary fixture backup restores account login/session-key consistency and owned submission history without copying unrelated files.
A partial/corrupted/missing-key backup is rejected before overwriting destination state.
Backup files are private, no credential values print, and generated archives remain excluded from Git and application packaging.
validation: Run the new backup/restore helper only against temporary fixture databases and a fresh temporary destination.
out_of_scope: Backing up production data without operator authorization
issues.risk: Backups contain credentials and source; accidental publication or destructive restore is a high-impact failure.

issues.title: Introduce versioned transactional migrations for the submission database
issues.problem: The submission store initializes tables with CREATE IF NOT EXISTS but has no recorded schema version or tested forward migration path. Retention, provenance and deletion changes need safe evolution of existing user data.
scope: Add a small schema-version registry and ordered transactional migrations for the existing SQLite store.
Represent the current schema as the supported baseline and fail safely on unknown newer versions.
Provide operator preflight/backup guidance and a failure rollback strategy without editing Better Auth-owned schema.
acceptance: A fixture built with the current schema upgrades without losing IDs, ownership, source, idempotency or lease semantics.
A failing migration leaves the prior valid schema/data intact; repeat startup does not reapply an already completed migration.
A database with a future unknown schema is refused with a safe diagnostic instead of silently modified.
out_of_scope: Writing custom migrations for Better Auth internal tables
Running destructive downgrade on real data
issues.risk: Schema mistakes can corrupt private history; require backup and real old-schema fixtures, not only fresh-database tests.

issues.title: Add a testable email-verification delivery flow for pilot accounts
issues.problem: Local email/password accounts do not verify email ownership. A real-user pilot needs a deliberate verification policy before relying on an email address for identity or recovery.
scope: Use Better Auth supported verification hooks with a delivery adapter and local deterministic outbox fixture.
Implement pending, resend, expired-link and verified UI states without confirming whether arbitrary addresses are registered.
Keep delivery disabled or local-only until the owner supplies an approved provider/configuration; no paid call by default.
acceptance: A fresh token verifies only its intended address once; expired/reused/mismatched tokens fail safely.
Resend is bounded and response wording does not enumerate accounts.
Verified-email requirements follow the approved pilot policy and do not silently lock out existing local development users.
out_of_scope: Selecting or purchasing a mail provider without approval
Sending real verification messages during tests
issues.risk: Mail links and logs can leak account tokens; use fixture delivery and library-supported semantics.

issues.title: Implement password recovery with bounded single-use reset links
issues.problem: There is no delivered account recovery flow. Users who lose a password cannot safely recover a pilot account through the current interface.
scope: Use supported Better Auth reset hooks and the verified delivery abstraction from B014.
Add request/reset views with neutral account-existence wording, resend limits and explicit expired-link behavior.
Apply the approved session invalidation policy on reset and disclose the existing short-lived API-token window unless separately changed.
acceptance: A valid reset link changes the intended account password once; used/expired links cannot be replayed.
Reset requests for absent/present addresses have indistinguishable public response structure.
The old password fails after reset; session behavior matches the documented policy, and no reset token is logged or persisted in browser storage.
out_of_scope: Guaranteeing immediate revocation of already issued stateless API JWTs without an explicit design
issues.risk: Enumeration and reset-link leakage can turn recovery into account takeover; use official library flows and adversarial fixtures.

issues.title: Expose owned session listing and revoke-other-sessions controls
issues.problem: The account page provides sign-out but no way to inspect or revoke other active sessions. Users cannot react deliberately to an unfamiliar session after an access concern.
scope: Use Better Auth supported session listing/revocation APIs and render a bounded owner-only session list.
Require recent authentication for revoke-other-sessions and identify the current session without revealing raw session tokens.
Show the documented limit that previously issued short-lived API tokens may remain usable for their remaining lifetime.
acceptance: Account A cannot list or revoke Account B sessions by supplying another identifier.
Revoking another session makes that cookie fail while the chosen current session remains usable.
Session token values never appear in DOM, API snapshots, logs or exports, and stale list responses are cleared on account change.
out_of_scope: Fingerprint-based identity or precise location tracking
issues.risk: Session metadata is sensitive, and stale browser state must not cross identities.

issues.title: Record privacy-safe account security events
issues.problem: The project has no owner-facing security activity history for password recovery, session revocation or account administration. Operators and users need limited evidence without storing credentials or excessive personal data.
scope: Define a small versioned security-event vocabulary and retention policy for completed recovery/session actions.
Record only approved metadata and expose a bounded owner-only activity list through supported account hooks.
Avoid raw token, password, mail-link, full IP or user-agent logging unless separately justified and approved.
acceptance: Fixtures produce exactly the intended event for reset/revocation success and distinguish failure without storing secret input.
A second user cannot query another account activity, and pagination/retention bounds are enforced.
The privacy document names stored fields and retention; event ingestion cannot be used for arbitrary log injection.
out_of_scope: A general SIEM or analytics platform
Claiming activity logs identify an attacker
issues.risk: Additional audit data creates privacy and storage obligations; collect the smallest useful record.

issues.title: Implement deliberate account deletion across auth and owned submission state
issues.problem: There is no end-to-end account deletion lifecycle. Removing only an auth row would strand private source/history, while deleting active work without coordination could break worker leases.
scope: Implement an explicitly confirmed, recently authenticated account deletion flow using supported identity hooks and owner-scoped API cleanup.
Apply the approved in-flight-job, retention and backup policy; refuse or defer unsafe active deletion rather than orphaning work.
Make retries idempotent and explain what is removed immediately versus retained temporarily by policy.
acceptance: The requester cannot target a different account; forged identity, stale reauthentication and CSRF attempts fail.
Deleting an eligible account removes or irreversibly anonymizes its approved live data classes without affecting another owner.
Interrupted/retried deletion converges to one documented terminal state; active jobs follow the stated safe policy and credentials are invalidated as supported.
out_of_scope: Deleting live user data during development validation
Promising instant erasure from historical backups without policy support
issues.risk: Deletion is destructive and spans two stores; fixtures and failure recovery must prove ownership and partial-completion behavior.

issues.title: Bound general API admission and concurrent slow requests
issues.problem: The current 128 KiB body and per-operation deadline do not bound simultaneous callers or whole-process request admission. Submission quotas alone cannot prevent general ingress exhaustion.
scope: Add a configurable bounded admission/concurrency policy appropriate to the existing single-process pilot, with clear limitations for multiple replicas.
Ensure slow bodies and slow auth requests release capacity on cancellation/timeouts.
Use safe overload responses and explicit retry information; preserve separate internal-worker capacity or a documented isolation policy.
acceptance: A deterministic concurrent-request fixture reaches the configured cap and receives bounded overload responses rather than unbounded work.
Cancelled and timed-out requests release permits; the next legitimate request succeeds.
Worker control traffic cannot be starved indefinitely by public catalog requests, and overload output includes no request body or credential.
validation: uv run --project services/api --frozen pytest services/api/tests/catalog/test_api.py services/api/tests/identity/test_auth.py
out_of_scope: Using caller-supplied identities as trusted rate-limit keys
issues.risk: An in-process cap is not a global multi-replica budget; document deployment scope and avoid self-deadlock on internal work.

issues.title: Add structured redacted request and failure logs
issues.problem: Request IDs and safe client errors exist, but there is no defined structured operational logging contract. Troubleshooting needs correlation and failure categories without exposing source, tokens or hidden cases.
scope: Define structured request/failure fields such as service, generated correlation ID, route template, duration and safe error category.
Redact or exclude authorization/cookies, raw query values, source, grading inputs, provider context and account identifiers beyond approved pseudonymous correlation.
Document output format and retention/collection assumptions without provisioning a paid logging service.
acceptance: Fixtures containing marker secrets in headers/body/query produce no marker in log output or exception formatting.
A failed request can be correlated with its safe response request ID and route template.
Untrusted multiline input cannot forge a second log record; logging failure does not change a valid API result.
out_of_scope: Publishing private source or security diagnostics
issues.risk: Logs are another data export channel; redaction must be tested before deployment collection is enabled.

issues.title: Expose private bounded operational readiness and queue metrics
issues.problem: Public health only reports process liveness and capabilities report recent worker readiness. Operators lack a private bounded view of queue age, expired leases and storage pressure without inspecting user records.
scope: Add an operator-only metrics/readiness surface that reuses trusted store state and does not return source, tests, bearer material or high-cardinality identifiers.
Separate liveness, deployment readiness and worker execution availability so a missing optional local judge is not mislabeled an API crash.
Document scrape/authentication and metric cardinality bounds; keep public responses minimal.
acceptance: Anonymous/learner credentials cannot read private operational metrics.
Seeded queued/running/expired fixtures yield exact aggregate counts and oldest-job age, with no source or user IDs.
Metrics collection remains bounded and unavailable storage produces a safe readiness failure rather than a false healthy state.
out_of_scope: Installing Prometheus or paid monitoring by default
issues.risk: Operator endpoints can expose sensitive topology and state; require a separate credential/policy and low-cardinality output.

issues.title: Apply retention to terminal submission source with a dry-run purge
issues.problem: Terminal private source/history grows indefinitely. The store has no approved source retention lifecycle, even when account/request quotas are respected.
scope: Implement the owner-approved source/summary retention policy for terminal records with an explicit dry-run report and bounded batches.
Preserve active jobs and any data classes the approved policy must retain; define idempotency behavior for purged source.
Run purge only through an authorized operator path or scheduled process with safe counts and no source output.
acceptance: Boundary-time fixtures purge only eligible terminal data and retain queued/running/other-owner records as specified.
Dry-run performs no writes and reports only aggregate counts/bytes; repeat purge is idempotent.
Detail/history endpoints handle a retained summary with expired source honestly instead of reconstructing or leaking content.
validation: Exercise the purge dry-run and apply paths only on temporary fixture databases.
out_of_scope: Deleting real developer/user history during validation
issues.risk: Retention is deliberate destruction; ensure policy, exclusions and backup behavior are explicit before enabling scheduled writes.

issues.title: Enforce cumulative owned-source storage budgets at submission admission
issues.problem: Per-source size and request/concurrency quotas do not bound cumulative stored source. A valid account can accumulate completed submissions until the shared disk is exhausted.
scope: Track or compute bounded per-owner retained-source usage transactionally and apply configured byte/record ceilings when accepting new submissions.
Keep idempotent replay of an existing request stable and exclude already purged bytes consistently.
Return an actionable safe quota error without revealing another account usage.
acceptance: Concurrent writes near the limit cannot exceed the configured budget by racing.
An idempotency-key replay returns the original record without double-charging usage; a conflicting replay retains its existing rejection.
After eligible retention frees bytes, a new request can be accepted, and another owner budget is unaffected.
issues.risk: Accounting races can bypass budgets or reject valid replay; enforce charging in the same transaction as creation.

issues.title: Avoid loading private source for submission summary pages
issues.problem: History listing uses SELECT * and constructs full details before discarding source. Large retained programs are unnecessarily read and materialized for summary-only pagination.
scope: Select explicit summary columns in the list query and map summaries without building SubmissionDetail.
Retain stable created_at/id ordering, owner filtering, total count and expiry semantics.
Add a regression fixture with large source to distinguish summary projection from detail retrieval.
acceptance: History responses are byte-for-byte contract-compatible and never include source_code.
An instrumented query/row fixture shows list mapping does not request/read the source_code column, while owned detail still returns it.
Pagination ties, empty pages and cross-owner access retain existing behavior.
out_of_scope: A database rewrite or ORM migration
issues.risk: Summary optimization must not bypass expiry/ownership checks or change deterministic pagination.

issues.title: Export an authenticated user-owned submission history bundle
issues.problem: Users can inspect individual owned attempts but cannot take a bounded portable export of their history. An export must honor retention and avoid becoming a cross-user or bulk-memory leak.
scope: Define a versioned owner export schema with attempts and optional retained source; use bounded batches and an explicit maximum/export continuation policy.
Add an authenticated download action and make expired-source omissions explicit.
Exclude tokens, internal worker IDs/leases, private grading cases and raw auth database content.
acceptance: Account A export contains only A records, even with supplied IDs or concurrent account changes.
A dataset exceeding the batch size exports completely through the documented bounded mechanism without materializing arbitrary history in one response.
Exported metadata identifies schema/time and omitted expired source; files contain no credentials or private test fields.
out_of_scope: Exporting all users or auth secrets
issues.risk: Exports are private source artifacts; owner authorization, response limits and cache/download handling need explicit tests.

issues.title: Extend problem provenance with explicit permitted-use metadata
issues.problem: Problem provenance currently records only author/source text. More content needs a machine-readable distinction between original authorship, permission, redistribution and training rights.
scope: Define a bounded public provenance schema with stable content identity, author attribution and approved permitted-use fields; keep private evidence references out of public responses.
Populate truthful metadata for the three original seed exercises without importing third-party banks.
Render concise attribution/rights information and validate it in the typed browser contract.
acceptance: Every current seed validates with explicit provenance; unknown/unapproved reuse states cannot silently become approved.
Public responses expose no private license documents or contributor personal contact data.
Malformed/oversized metadata is rejected and existing problem rendering/tests remain contract-compatible through an intentional schema change.
out_of_scope: Inventing legal permission for public websites
issues.risk: Rights metadata is a recorded authorization, not automatic legal clearance; owner/content review is required.

issues.title: Version problem and grader identity on every new submission
issues.problem: Submissions retain problem slug/title but not an immutable public specification and grading revision. Future content changes could make an old verdict appear to refer to a different problem/test contract.
scope: Introduce explicit problem revision and grader-manifest identity at creation/lease time without exposing private cases.
Persist these identities in new submissions via a tested migration and define how legacy records are labeled unknown/legacy.
Require the worker to reject unsupported revision combinations safely rather than grade with the nearest current slug.
acceptance: Changing current problem content does not relabel the revision recorded on an existing attempt.
A worker cannot complete an unsupported revision as AC; the job receives a safe explicit system outcome.
Owned history/detail and exports show revision metadata, while private grading content remains outside public API/model context.
out_of_scope: Building a full contest/version administration platform
Returning hidden test data or expected answers
issues.risk: Revision mismatches can silently invalidate verdicts; worker/API identity must be checked before execution and preserved in records.

issues.title: Detect public-sample drift between catalog and judge deployments
issues.problem: Public samples are represented across independent API/judge deployments. Current examples can drift so Run samples checks a different input/output from the problem page.
scope: Add a deterministic public-only sample manifest or cross-component contract fixture keyed by problem revision.
Compare exact sample inputs/outputs and supported language starter interfaces without coupling API imports to private judge test data.
Document how an author updates both deployments and how mismatch blocks release.
acceptance: All three current problems have identical public sample contracts across API and judge.
Changing one sample fixture on either side causes a targeted consistency failure with problem/revision identification.
The shared/public fixture contains no generated private grading cases or oracle answers beyond public samples.
out_of_scope: Merging trusted private grading data into the API package
Executing arbitrary author code on the API host
issues.risk: A shared manifest must not accidentally package private tests into web/API artifacts.

issues.title: Validate trusted problem authoring inputs before catalog publication
issues.problem: Catalog exercises are hand-authored in Python source. Adding content lacks a focused author preflight for duplicate IDs/slugs, incomplete constraints, bad samples, missing provenance or revision mismatch.
scope: Create an offline trusted-author validation command for the existing content format or a deliberately small versioned input format.
Check identifier uniqueness, required statements/formats/constraints, sample shape, starter languages, hint levels, provenance and public/grader revision linkage.
Report path/field errors without executing arbitrary uploaded scripts or ingesting external archives.
acceptance: The current seeds pass all documented checks, while fixtures for duplicate slug, missing rights, invalid sample and revision mismatch fail precisely.
The command leaves input files unchanged and never imports a user-selected executable module.
An author can follow one documented workflow to prepare a reviewed content PR with B001 evidence.
validation: Run the new authoring command only on trusted committed seeds and intentionally invalid temporary data fixtures.
issues.risk: An authoring validator must validate data rather than become an unrestricted code loader.

issues.title: Add one original prefix-sum range-query teaching exercise
issues.problem: The three current seeds cover summation, contiguous growth and sliding windows. There is no original exercise teaching preprocessing with repeated range queries.
scope: Author one original statement, constraints, two informative public samples, Python/C++17 starter code and three progressive authored hints.
Add a small independent reference oracle and generated boundary cases for one-based/zero-based endpoints, full-range queries, negatives and 64-bit totals.
Use the provenance, revision and authoring gates already introduced; keep expected private cases in the trusted judge.
acceptance: A correct Python and C++17 solution receive AC on the authorized finite tests; off-by-one and repeated-linear-scan fixtures demonstrate the intended failure limits.
Both public samples agree with the independent oracle and the rendered statement.
The content has explicit original authorship and no copied third-party problem text; explanation states O(n+q) reasoning without a universal-correctness claim.
validation: In a supported isolated runtime: npm run test:judge:integration
out_of_scope: Claiming finite grading proves all-input correctness
issues.risk: Poor constraints/oracles can invalidate teaching and verdicts; require independent content review.

issues.title: Use bounded server-side pagination for the expanding problem catalog
issues.problem: The UI currently fetches limit=100 once and filters that page locally. Once the catalog exceeds the first page, learners could miss matching problems while totals imply a larger searchable collection.
scope: Drive bounded q/difficulty/tag/limit/offset requests through the existing catalog API instead of pretending the first 100 entries are the whole library.
Add deliberate pagination/loading/empty states, cancel stale searches and reset offset when filters change.
Retain the simple existing API store and avoid adding search infrastructure.
acceptance: A fixture with more than 100 problems finds a matching item beyond the original first page.
Rapid filter changes cannot render stale results or retain an out-of-range offset.
Displayed totals, page boundaries and empty results match API semantics; keyboard access and existing retry behavior remain usable.
out_of_scope: Unbounded client fetching of the entire catalog
issues.risk: Stale network responses and partial-page filtering can create misleading results; retain strict schemas and cancellation.

issues.title: Make catalog filters and page position shareable through the URL
issues.problem: Search, difficulty and topic exist only in component state. Refresh, browser navigation and shared links lose the chosen practice view.
scope: Map supported filter/page values to validated query parameters and restore them on initial navigation.
Update browser history intentionally without placing sensitive data in the URL.
Normalize unknown/overlong values and provide an accessible clear-filters action that resets the URL and pagination together.
acceptance: A copied filtered URL restores the same API query and visible result set after reload.
Back/forward navigation restores the previous valid filter state without duplicate stale fetches.
Invalid or overlong parameters are normalized safely, and no source, token or account ID enters the URL.
issues.risk: URL state must be bounded and must not introduce navigation loops or expose private drafts.

issues.title: Add explicit local draft export and bounded import
issues.problem: Drafts are best-effort browser storage and learners are told to copy their code, but there is no deliberate portable download/import path when storage fails or a browser is replaced.
scope: Add user-initiated source download with clear problem/language file naming.
Add a bounded plain-text import flow with preview and explicit replace confirmation; do not execute or upload imported content.
Preserve the current Monaco/simple-editor and storage-failure behavior.
acceptance: Exported UTF-8 bytes match the selected draft exactly, including non-ASCII text and trailing newline.
An oversized or unsupported import is rejected before changing the draft; cancel preserves the original bytes.
Import/export work in the simple-editor fallback and cause no submission, model request or external network call.
issues.risk: Import is a destructive edit and export may contain private source; require explicit user intent and bounded text handling.

issues.title: Offer explicit draft ownership and clear-on-shared-device controls
issues.problem: The current draft key is scoped by browser/problem/language, not by signed-in account. The disclosure is honest, but shared-device users have no deliberate account-scoping or local-clear workflow.
scope: Define separate guest and signed-in local namespaces without treating localStorage as encrypted account backup.
Offer explicit export/keep/move choices for existing guest drafts and a bounded clear-local-drafts control.
Never silently upload drafts or erase another browser identity on sign-out; explain shared-device behavior.
acceptance: Switching A to B cannot silently display A private draft under B namespace.
Existing v1 guest drafts remain recoverable until the user chooses migration or deletion; cancelled prompts preserve bytes.
Clear-local-drafts affects only the selected namespace and explicit confirmation; no server source is deleted or uploaded.
out_of_scope: Claiming browser storage is encrypted or secure against local device access
issues.risk: Local identity migration can lose code or cross account boundaries; migration must be reversible through explicit export.

issues.title: Detect cross-tab draft conflicts before overwriting newer code
issues.problem: Two tabs editing the same local draft overwrite one storage key without revision metadata or a conflict warning. A stale tab can silently replace more recent code.
scope: Record a small local draft revision/timestamp envelope with a migration path for plain v1 text.
Observe storage events for the active namespace and show a non-destructive conflict choice when another tab changes the saved revision.
Keep each unsaved in-memory value available for copying/export before choosing one version.
acceptance: Two-tab fixtures trigger a conflict notice instead of silently overwriting a newer saved revision.
Choosing keep-local, load-other or cancel has deterministic storage/editor outcomes and preserves an exportable losing version until explicit resolution.
Different problem/language/account namespaces do not trigger conflicts, and storage-unavailable fallback still permits editing.
out_of_scope: Pretending timestamps provide distributed conflict-free correctness
issues.risk: Migration must not mistake existing source text for malformed metadata or discard unsaved code.

issues.title: Add persistent editor display and accessibility preferences
issues.problem: The editor exposes basic mode/reset controls but no deliberate learner control over font size, wrapping or preferred simple-editor mode. These choices affect readability and keyboard accessibility.
scope: Add a small bounded preference model for font size, wrapping and editor mode using local non-sensitive storage.
Apply compatible behavior to Monaco and the simple editor, with a reset-to-default action.
Keep preferences separate from source drafts and handle unavailable/malformed storage safely.
acceptance: Preferences survive reload and apply consistently without changing source bytes or submission language.
Out-of-range/malformed saved preferences fall back to supported defaults.
Controls have accessible names, keyboard operation and usable focus; choosing simple mode does not repeatedly force Monaco back.
issues.risk: Preference initialization can race draft hydration; source must remain unchanged.

issues.title: Complete keyboard navigation for the practice and submission workflow
issues.problem: Basic keyboard support exists, but there is no complete documented keyboard-only path through navigation, problem reading, editor entry/exit, language selection, hints and deliberate submission.
scope: Audit the existing flow with a keyboard and repair concrete focus-order, editor-escape and visible-focus gaps.
Add a skip-to-main/editor guidance path without trapping Tab inside Monaco or inventing mandatory shortcuts.
Document supported editor behavior and add focused browser assertions for repaired gaps.
acceptance: A keyboard-only fixture reaches and operates catalog, problem, editor, language and Run/Submit controls without pointer input.
Users can leave both Monaco and simple editor through a documented accessible mechanism; focus is never trapped.
Disabled/loading/retry controls expose state and visible focus remains discernible in supported themes.
validation: Record a manual keyboard pass for the exact changed workflow; do not claim full WCAG conformance.
issues.risk: Automation cannot establish all editor assistive-technology behavior; include an actual manual pass and limitations.

issues.title: Improve screen-reader announcements and focus for asynchronous results
issues.problem: The app uses role=status/alert in places, but there is no reviewed announcement/focus contract across account errors, hint retry, polled verdicts and opened history details. Repeated polling can be noisy or updates can be missed.
scope: Define concise live-region announcements for meaningful state changes, with stable labels and error associations.
Preserve logical focus after retries, modal/confirmation actions and detail opening; avoid shifting focus on every poll.
Add targeted assertions and a manual screen-reader walkthrough for repaired cases.
acceptance: One transition to a final verdict announces once; unchanged polls do not repeat the same message indefinitely.
Account field/error relationships and hint result provenance are programmatically exposed.
After retry/detail close or account change, focus remains on a meaningful visible control and stale private result text is removed.
validation: Record manual screen-reader/keyboard findings for the affected states, including the tool/version used.
out_of_scope: Claiming automated checks replace assistive-technology review
issues.risk: Over-announcement and forced focus can make a technically labeled UI unusable; test real interaction timing.

issues.title: Repair contrast, reduced-motion and zoom reflow gaps
issues.problem: Responsive styles exist, but the repository has no demonstrated review of text/control contrast, reduced-motion behavior and high-zoom reflow. Decorative motion and narrow result surfaces can block access.
scope: Measure contrast of actual text/control/focus states and repair specific failures without redesigning the product.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion for decorative animation and smooth scrolling.
Check 200%/400% zoom and a narrow viewport for catalog, problem/editor controls and result text; preserve necessary code scrolling without page-wide loss of controls.
acceptance: Changed text/control combinations meet the chosen documented WCAG AA contrast criterion with recorded measurements.
Reduced-motion emulation removes nonessential animation while all controls remain usable.
At reviewed zoom/viewports, content and actions are reachable with no clipped critical labels or horizontal page scrolling caused by layout controls.
validation: Record manual contrast and zoom findings for changed states and limitations.
out_of_scope: Reformatting user code to eliminate editor horizontal scrolling
issues.risk: Visual fixes can hide controls or alter editor sizing; preserve responsive behavior and clear focus states.

issues.title: Add a focused automated accessibility regression gate
issues.problem: Accessibility repairs need a repeatable regression signal. Existing functional Playwright assertions do not provide a dedicated scan of representative guest, signed-in, loading, error and result states.
scope: Review and pin a browser accessibility scanner as a development-only dependency, retaining its license and lockfile integrity.
Scan a small representative set of stable app states and fail on agreed actionable violations; keep explicit, justified exceptions narrow.
Document which manual keyboard/screen-reader checks remain necessary and attach evidence to AI-authored PRs.
acceptance: A deliberate missing-label or contrast fixture is detected by the new gate and a clean repaired state passes.
The gate covers guest practice, account form, authored hint result and owned submission result without scanning private production data.
Exceptions identify a specific rule/node, reason and owner rather than globally disabling categories; scan output does not claim full conformance.
validation: Run the scoped Playwright accessibility cases added to the existing practice/hints/submissions suites.
When CI execution is authorized, observe the dedicated accessibility job/step on the exact PR commit.
out_of_scope: Adding a paid audit service by default
Globally suppressing violations to obtain a green check
issues.risk: Scanner version changes and noisy exceptions can erode trust; pin the tool and review exceptions like code.

issues.title: Persist owned sandbox records and reconcile crash-orphaned containers
issues.problem: The corrected runner retains failed cleanup names in _active and stops readiness, but that set disappears if the worker process crashes. A restart cannot distinguish its leftover sandboxes from unrelated containers, and the existing incident exercise does not implement recovery authority.
scope: Introduce a minimal private, atomically persisted sandbox-ownership journal written before container creation and cleared only after confirmed absence. Store generated container identity, approved image identity and lifecycle generation; never store source, test input, account identifiers or bearer material.

Label newly created sandboxes with the same trusted ownership generation. On startup, perform one bounded reconciliation pass that validates both journal and actual container labels/image before removing an owned orphan.
Treat malformed journal data, mismatched ownership, unreachable Docker and unresolved cleanup as unavailable readiness with sanitized diagnostics; preserve the record for an explicit operator retry.
acceptance: A simulated crash after create and before normal cleanup leaves a recoverable record; a fresh runner instance removes only the matching owned sandbox before becoming ready.
An unrelated container or a journal entry with a mismatched ownership label/image is never removed automatically and cannot grant readiness.
Journal permissions, atomic replacement, bounded size and redacted failure output are exercised; duplicate reconciliation is safe and no host execution fallback exists.
validation: On an explicitly approved isolated gVisor test host, run a finite one-container crash/restart fixture and record cleanup plus unchanged unrelated-container identity.
out_of_scope: Sweeping every Docker container or deleting unknown state
Persisting private program data or worker secrets
issues.risk: Automatic orphan cleanup is destructive unless ownership is established independently of an untrusted filename or container name; refuse ambiguous recovery.

issues.title: Bind controller credentials to registered worker identities
issues.problem: require_worker currently authenticates one shared bearer, while heartbeat, lease and completion accept a caller-supplied worker_id. Any holder belongs to the entire controller trust domain and can register or impersonate another worker; token-strength and rotation tasks do not establish separate principals.
scope: Resolve an authenticated controller credential to one owner-registered stable worker principal and bind every internal route payload to that principal rather than trusting worker_id alone.

Retain a bounded per-principal current/previous credential overlap using the rotation mechanism from B010; provide an explicit single-worker development configuration rather than an implicit production shared-key fallback.

Reject unknown identities and cross-principal heartbeat, lease and completion operations with closed safe errors; document credential provisioning and revocation without writing actual secrets into Git.
acceptance: Two configured worker fixtures can operate only under their registered identities; the credential for A cannot register, renew, lease as or complete a lease belonging to B.
Rotating or revoking A leaves B unaffected and preserves only the deliberately allowed bounded overlap for A.
The normal configured single-worker local workflow remains supported, while production mode refuses an unbound shared credential; no secret appears in logs or capability output.
out_of_scope: Building a certificate authority or automatic worker registration service
Rotating real deployment credentials without operator approval
Treating per-worker identity as protection against a malicious trusted Docker host
issues.risk: An identity migration can lock out valid workers or accidentally widen completion rights; use explicit compatibility and cross-principal denial fixtures.
issues.owner_role: Backend security engineer and judge maintainer

issues.title: Enforce an atomic active-lease allowance per worker principal
issues.problem: The current worker implementation runs serially, but the API lease transaction has no check for an existing RUNNING lease belonging to the worker. Repeated or concurrent authenticated lease requests can reserve many jobs, so the client convention is not an enforceable execution allowance.
scope: Inside the existing atomic lease transaction, enforce a configured active-lease allowance for the authenticated worker principal; begin with the current one-job-per-worker contract.
Return a documented busy/no-new-lease outcome without claiming another job, and release allowance only after the authoritative completion or expiry transition.
Keep idempotent retry and cross-worker ownership semantics explicit; integrate with registered identities from B122 so inventing another worker_id cannot evade the allowance.
acceptance: Two concurrent lease calls for the same principal cannot create more RUNNING jobs than its configured allowance.
A busy worker does not consume another queued job; a second independently authorized worker can lease its own job.
Completion and lease expiry each release exactly the intended allowance, while stale completion and forged identity do not release or consume another worker slot.
out_of_scope: Changing learner submission quotas or provider budgets
Assuming a lease count measures actual CPU or aggregate memory
issues.risk: A nontransactional count-and-lease check can race; a stranded lease must expire without allowing cross-worker or double completion.

issues.title: Gate production readiness on an approved supported runtime identity
issues.problem: Preflight establishes that runsc exists, rootless Docker is selected and finite probes pass. It does not enforce a maintained approved runtime identity or support window. The historical review explicitly records an outdated installed runtime; B111 qualifies candidates later but does not establish this prerequisite policy.
scope: Record an owner/operator-approved production runtime support policy: trusted deployment inventory source, approved runtime/image identities, review owner, review deadline and rollback identity.

Require production startup/diagnostics to validate the current daemon runtime identity against that approved inventory. An unverifiable identity or expired review must prevent readiness rather than infer patch status from the word runsc.

Keep operator deployment/update actions separate from application configuration. Feed the approved policy into the existing B111 canary qualification work instead of creating another upgrade rehearsal.
acceptance: Fixtures for approved, unapproved, unverifiable and expired-review identities produce explicit safe readiness outcomes.
Diagnostics distinguish declared identity, independently available runtime evidence and unknown provenance; hashing a local binary is not mislabeled proof of a remote daemon runtime.
No host package is installed or runtime replaced by application startup, and documented development-only use of an older managed runtime cannot be described as production patched.
validation: Statically review the operator-approved runtime policy and inventory provenance; a real production approval cannot be invented by a coding agent.
out_of_scope: A second canary implementation duplicating B111
Independent sandbox certification or guaranteed freedom from vulnerabilities
issues.risk: A self-asserted or stale inventory can create false confidence; policy approval and actual deployment evidence must have a named operator and expiry.
issues.owner_role: Judge operator, security reviewer and project owner

issues.title: Require a verified aggregate resource envelope for a production judge host
issues.problem: The present managed rootless runtime lacks aggregate cgroup memory/PID accounting. Per-process rlimits and per-container tmpfs caps are real finite controls, but adding workers can exceed host-wide CPU, memory, process or temporary-storage budgets. B109 measures capacity; it does not enforce these limits.
scope: Define one explicit operator-provisioned dedicated-host production resource envelope, including aggregate CPU, memory, PID, running-sandbox and temporary-storage ceilings; preserve the current bounded development mode as a clearly separate mode.

Add production preflight that verifies supported aggregate controls and the selected host/cgroup assignment before advertising readiness. Pass only reviewed fixed resource arguments to Docker and retain existing per-process, no-network and output controls.

Fail production readiness when accounting/enforcement cannot be verified or owned orphan usage exceeds the declared envelope. Do not install or reconfigure the managed daemon or claim that a CLI flag alone proves enforcement.
acceptance: Mocked unsupported/missing/mismatched aggregate-control states refuse production readiness and cannot silently select the development policy.

On an approved dedicated test host, finite original multi-process/concurrent sandbox fixtures demonstrate the declared aggregate caps and controlled recovery; report which resource dimensions were actually measured.
The supported development configuration retains its explicit limitations, and no new accurate-MLE or sandbox-certification claim is made without trustworthy evidence.
validation: Run only the new explicitly enabled, finite aggregate-budget fixtures on an operator-approved dedicated gVisor host; mark them blocked rather than passed on the current unsupported managed runtime.
out_of_scope: Provisioning paid hosts or changing the cloud daemon automatically
A multi-host scheduler or unlimited stress testing
Claiming protection from --memory or --pids-limit when the daemon reports no enforcement
issues.risk: Resource flags can be ignored by unsupported runtimes; readiness must depend on observed controls, not desired configuration. Host provisioning remains an external operator prerequisite.
issues.owner_role: Judge infrastructure engineer and security reviewer

issues.title: Withdraw worker readiness and reconcile its current lease on retirement
issues.problem: Cleanup failure now stops further claims and heartbeat renewal, but the API can continue advertising the last worker heartbeat for 60 seconds. Process/transport failure also leaves lease retirement to expiry. There is no explicit generation-bound withdrawal protocol connecting shutdown, cleanup outcome and the authoritative lease state.
scope: Add one authenticated principal-and-instance-bound retirement operation using a closed reason vocabulary. Atomically withdraw only that worker instance from availability and prevent further lease grants.

Have graceful shutdown or revoked runtime readiness attempt this operation with a short fixed deadline while still preserving controlled in-flight completion and orphan records. A transport failure retains the existing expiry fallback.

Specify an idempotent authoritative disposition for its current lease: retain an already committed terminal result; otherwise record only a safe SYSTEM_ERROR when retirement is authorized, and never auto-requeue code whose cleanup is unconfirmed.
acceptance: Successful retirement removes the affected worker from capabilities immediately while other ready workers remain available.
A late heartbeat/retirement from a previous process generation cannot revive or retire its registered replacement, and another worker principal cannot affect the lease.

Shutdown versus completion races yield exactly one documented terminal state with no private diagnostics, no second execution and no hung shutdown; unavailable retirement transport falls back to the documented finite heartbeat/lease expiry behavior.
out_of_scope: Assuming API retirement proves a container was removed
issues.risk: Retiring a shared identity or releasing an uncertain lease incorrectly can invalidate a healthy replacement or double-execute code; principal, process generation and lease transitions must be checked transactionally.
issues.owner_role: Backend queue engineer and judge maintainer

issues.title: Add a bounded metrics exporter consuming the existing private operational surface
issues.problem: Once B021 supplies canonical private queue/readiness measurements, operators need a stable low-cardinality exporter/report adapter without a second metrics authority.
scope: Consume B021 aggregate measurements through its existing authenticated operator boundary; do not create another queue/readiness endpoint.
Add a versioned bounded export adapter for outcome/latency histograms and worker health, with an explicitly reviewed scrape/rotation policy.
Reuse B020 redaction and cardinality rules; keep user/source/token data out of metrics.
acceptance: Exporter fixtures match B021 canonical counters and handle unhealthy/stale input honestly.
No second metrics endpoint, competing source of truth or unbounded identity labels are introduced.
Unauthorized scrapes and unavailable source state fail safely without exposing underlying data.
issues.risk: Metrics labels and endpoints can leak private activity or overload storage.

issues.title: Propagate redacted correlation identifiers across accepted jobs
issues.problem: Request-level diagnostics are difficult to connect to leased jobs and worker completion safely.
scope: Carry B020 existing server-generated request correlation ID into accepted job, worker lease and sanitized completion lineage.
Validate length/format and use bounded diagnostics; identifiers remain telemetry and cannot grant ownership or select hidden tests.
Reuse the existing log/telemetry schema instead of creating another request-ID authority.
acceptance: A request/job/worker fixture can be followed by one correlation identifier without including source or credentials.
Malformed and oversized supplied identifiers cannot inject log lines or labels.
Lease retries retain the intended job lineage while attempts remain distinguishable.
out_of_scope: Publishing internal identifiers in unrestricted public analytics
issues.risk: Improper correlation data can become an injection or cross-user tracking vector.

issues.title: Define measurable service objectives and test operator alert rules
issues.problem: A working local service does not define when operators should treat a deployment as degraded.
scope: Add proposed configuration/runbook rules for queue delay, stale workers, job-control failures and API error rate.
Create deterministic metric fixtures to exercise alert activation and recovery, with owner-selected thresholds.
acceptance: Each rule has an owner, observation window and tested firing/recovery fixture.
Expected learner WA/CE/RE outcomes do not count as application incidents.
A worker-readiness failure prevents an operator from declaring execution healthy.
out_of_scope: Unapproved external paging or paid monitoring
issues.risk: Noisy alerts can hide actual incidents; broad thresholds can miss failures.
issues.owner_role: Site reliability engineer and service owner

issues.title: Rehearse a timed full-stack disaster restore using the approved backup helper
issues.problem: B012 provides the backup/restore implementation; operations still need an isolated full-service recovery rehearsal with measured completeness and timing.
scope: Invoke B012 backup/restore tooling and manifest format in fresh disposable service volumes; do not create another backup format or restore implementation.
Restart web/API against restored data and verify auth/key continuity, ownership and job-recovery policy without changing live developer state.
Produce a redacted RPO/RTO rehearsal report against B003 targets, including interrupted/missing-generation cases.
acceptance: A seeded account can authenticate and read only its restored attempts after the drill restart.
Missing key material, corrupt backup and mismatched database generation cause a clear failure.
The report records measured restore duration and completeness, and proves original state was untouched.
out_of_scope: Designing the foundational backup storage/encryption system
Uploading backups to a new paid service
issues.risk: A partial restoration can lose accounts, invalidate sessions or mismatch ownership.
issues.owner_role: Site reliability engineer with privacy reviewer

issues.title: Measure bounded capacity and overload behavior using original fixtures
issues.problem: Queue limits need an empirical operating envelope before opening a pilot.
scope: Add a proposed opt-in load rehearsal with explicit concurrency/job/time ceilings and only original harmless programs.
Measure queue latency, rejection behavior, cancellations and recovery under the configured local/dedicated test environment.
acceptance: The run refuses to start without an explicit finite budget.
Over-capacity requests receive the documented bounded response and the queue drains after load stops.
A reproducible report records environment/revision and distinguishes measured limits from production guarantees.
out_of_scope: Paid load infrastructure or testing third-party endpoints
issues.risk: A careless load test can exhaust the shared development machine.

issues.title: Implement a revisioned deployment smoke and rollback rehearsal
issues.problem: Local builds alone do not prove a deployable revision can be promoted or rolled back safely.
scope: Add a proposed operator-invoked release rehearsal using immutable built artifact identifiers and isolated state.
Verify health, account/session continuity, owned history and compatibility before recording a promotion decision.
acceptance: A healthy candidate and a deliberately unhealthy candidate exercise promotion and rollback paths.
Rollback preserves seeded account/submission state and records the exact application/artifact revisions.
The helper never publishes externally or modifies the running environment without an explicit operator invocation.
out_of_scope: Provisioning a hosting account or paid infrastructure
issues.risk: Rollback across incompatible state versions can corrupt user data.

issues.title: Create a canary qualification gate for judge runtime upgrades
issues.problem: Maintaining isolation requires a repeatable way to evaluate a runtime/toolchain update before broad rollout.
scope: Add a proposed comparison runbook/report for an operator-provided approved candidate runtime or image.
Run existing hostile-program, cleanup and language fixtures on the candidate before allowing a canary decision.
acceptance: Reports name old/new runtime and image identifiers and every executed/skipped check.
A failed isolation/cleanup probe blocks qualification even when correct solutions pass.
The process does not replace the managed host daemon or silently fall back to ordinary containers.
issues.risk: A toolchain update can weaken isolation or alter resource semantics.

issues.title: Run a bounded incident exercise for worker outage and recovery
issues.problem: Operators need evidence that readiness, job reconciliation and user messaging work during failures.
scope: Add a proposed isolated exercise covering lost worker heartbeat, interrupted control service and restored service.
Record detection, containment, queued-job reconciliation and owner communication steps without sending external messages automatically.
acceptance: The exercise demonstrates unavailable execution while probes fail and safe recovery after reconciliation.
No attempt is attributed to another account or completed twice.
A post-exercise report names observed times, unresolved gaps and a responsible owner; live databases remain untouched.
out_of_scope: Simulated credential theft against real accounts
Automatic incident messaging or account-admin changes
issues.risk: An exercise that touches live state can create the incident it is meant to test.
issues.owner_role: Site reliability engineer and service owner

issues.title: Record the single-provider hint pilot activation decision
issues.problem: Authored hints and their UI work, but no provider, data-processing terms, spend owner or activation authority has been selected for real inference.
scope: Document one bounded hint pilot and its permitted public-only context.
Record provider-selection criteria, credential destinations, pricing assumptions, responsible owner and rollback authority.
Make activation conditional on privacy, admission and transport issues below.
acceptance: Decision separates authored service, optional model pilot and unapproved debugging/training.
Every unresolved credential, rights or spending prerequisite has an owner and blocks activation.
No default configuration begins paid inference.
validation: Document review against docs/status/PROJECT_STATUS.md and the existing HintBackend implementation; no provider calls.
out_of_scope: Provisioning a paid account or GPU
issues.risk: A written provider name must not be mistaken for permission to send user data or spend money.
issues.owner_role: Project owner with privacy and AI engineering reviewers

issues.title: Bound and fingerprint the existing public-only hint context
issues.problem: PublicHintContext already excludes private tests and identity, but future inference needs explicit per-field and aggregate bounds and a stable content fingerprint.
scope: Add validated context-size limits and deterministic canonical fingerprinting without introducing private grading fields.
Define overflow rejection or documented deterministic truncation for each public field.
Keep authored lookup behavior and the public HTTP v1 response compatible.
acceptance: Private test/source/credential sentinels never enter serialized model context.
Identical authorized catalog content produces the same fingerprint; changed samples change it.
Boundary and one-byte-over-limit inputs have deterministic outcomes.
validation: Future authorized check: uv run --project services/api --frozen pytest services/api/tests/hints -q
issues.risk: Silent truncation could remove a constraint and produce misleading hints.

issues.title: Validate trusted provider destinations and secret configuration
issues.problem: The authored-only selector intentionally fails closed. A future provider must not inherit archive adapters that accept arbitrary endpoints or ambiguous environment state.
scope: Define administrator-controlled HTTPS destination/model settings with strict URL parsing and an explicit local-development exception policy.
Reject URL userinfo, unexpected redirects and request-supplied endpoint overrides.
Validate credential presence without logging values; keep authored as the default.
acceptance: Malformed, unapproved and insecure external destinations fail before transport.
Missing credentials produce a sanitized configuration failure.
No browser bundle, OpenAPI example or log contains credential values.
validation: Future authorized check: uv run --project services/api --frozen pytest services/api/tests/hints -q
issues.risk: Provider configuration can become an SSRF or credential-forwarding boundary if endpoint control leaks to callers.

issues.title: Define an internal generation result and usage contract
issues.problem: HintBackend returns bounded HintContent today; real inference also needs trusted model identity, usage, finish reason and request metadata without exposing provider payloads.
scope: Introduce an internal provider-neutral result separating display content from operational metadata.
Represent missing usage, partial completion and unknown billing explicitly.
Adapt authored generation to the internal interface while preserving its truthful source/provider fields.
acceptance: Existing HTTP v1 authored responses remain compatible.
Operational metadata cannot serialize into the learner response accidentally.
Invalid provenance and contradictory usage/finish data are rejected by named contract rules.
validation: Future authorized check: uv run --project services/api --frozen pytest services/api/tests/hints -q
issues.risk: Treating absent provider usage as zero would undercount spend.

issues.title: Version bounded hint prompts and spoiler policies
issues.problem: The three authored levels have clear meaning; a model integration needs repeatable templates that preserve that progression instead of exposing full solutions by default.
scope: Define versioned concept/observation/plan templates and a minimal response format.
Treat problem text as quoted task data with no authority over permissions or tools.
Record prompt version with internal run metadata without requesting or storing hidden chain-of-thought.
acceptance: Each level has a reviewed allowed-content rubric and output limit.
Prompt-injection fixtures cannot add tools, destinations or private context.
Template changes alter a recorded version/fingerprint and keep authored content untouched.
validation: Future authorized check: uv run --project services/api --frozen pytest services/api/tests/hints -q; human review of level rubrics.
issues.risk: A model may still overshare; prompt instructions require output review and product policy.

issues.title: Reject malformed model hints before constructing learner responses
issues.problem: HintContent already bounds and labels authored/mock/model output, but raw provider responses need a separate defensive normalization boundary.
scope: Validate selected provider message content, completion status and text size before HintContent construction.
Reject empty, oversized, unexpected multimodal/tool-call and incomplete responses with stable sanitized errors.
Keep raw model text out of exception messages and logs.
acceptance: Every malformed-response fixture produces a stable failure rather than partial success.
Accepted model hints always have source=model, ai_generated=true and a configured provider identifier.
Existing frontend provenance/schema checks remain strict.
validation: Future authorized check: uv run --project services/api --frozen pytest services/api/tests/hints -q; npm run typecheck
issues.risk: String cleanup must not silently convert a refusal or truncated answer into a normal hint.

issues.title: Add deterministic provider transport fixtures without external inference
issues.problem: Real transport behavior cannot be validated by relabeling an authored hint or by requiring paid calls in routine checks.
scope: Create deterministic HTTP transport fixtures for success, refusal, malformed data, rate limiting and disconnects.
Assert exact outgoing field allowlists and absence of account JWTs, worker tokens, private tests and source.
Separate fixture provenance from actual model-backed production responses.
acceptance: Fixtures run with all outbound network access denied.
Tests fail when an extra credential/context field is injected.
No fixture result is presented as evidence of model quality or paid-provider access.
