validation: Future authorized check: uv run --project services/api --frozen pytest services/api/tests/hints -q
out_of_scope: Adding a public mock backend as a completed AI feature

issues.problem: Existing owned attempts cannot yet prove which contest, problem version or event window they belong to.
scope: Add a proposed optional contest context without changing ordinary practice behavior.
Bind event eligibility, authoritative receipt time, problem version and scoring identity atomically when accepting a request.
acceptance: Early, late, unregistered and mismatched-problem attempts are rejected before queuing.
Idempotent retries preserve one receipt time and one scored attempt.
Queued work finishing after the deadline is handled by the documented receipt-time policy; practice regression tests pass.
issues.risk: Race conditions between registration, deadline and enqueue could create unfair attempts.

issues.title: Implement isolated virtual-contest sessions with personal start times
issues.problem: A learner cannot replay a contest under a personal timer without changing the shared event.
scope: Add proposed virtual-session state referencing an immutable published problem set and duration.
Keep personal timing/scoring separate from official standings and provide a recoverable resume view.
acceptance: Two learners starting at different times receive independent deadlines and standings.
Reloading or opening a second tab cannot reset or extend a started session.
Virtual attempts never appear in official rankings.
issues.risk: Shared identifiers could mix personal and official attempts.

issues.title: Add locked ICPC team rosters and event membership rules
issues.problem: ICPC-style participation needs explicit team identity rather than caller-supplied teammate IDs.
scope: Implement proposed invitation, acceptance, captain and roster-lock rules for a contest team.
Enforce team-size limits and the policy for one user joining multiple teams in the same event.
acceptance: Only an invited account can accept its own invitation.
A locked roster rejects membership changes except the documented organizer correction.
Concurrent acceptance cannot exceed the configured team-size or single-team limit.
issues.risk: Membership races or invitation leakage could grant unintended team access.

issues.title: Scope contest attempts and source visibility to authorized team members
issues.problem: Existing submissions are individual-owned; team sharing must be deliberate and event-bounded.
scope: Add proposed team-scoring attribution and explicit source/history visibility rules for event members.
Preserve personal practice ownership and define access after roster correction or event completion.
acceptance: Eligible teammates can view only the event attempts allowed by policy.
A member of another team and a former unauthorized member cannot fetch source through detail/list endpoints.
The event scoreboard attributes retries and idempotent attempts to exactly one team.
issues.risk: Expanding ownership from a user to a team can leak private code.

issues.title: Enforce contest assistance policy across hint and submission routes
issues.problem: Contest rules require server-enforced assistance restrictions; hiding the hint panel is insufficient.
scope: Add proposed explicit event assistance modes and policy evaluation shared by relevant API entrypoints.
Show the effective policy in the workspace and permit post-event review only when event rules allow it.
acceptance: Direct authenticated requests cannot obtain disallowed assistance during a restricted event.
Allowed practice and post-event modes retain correct authored/model provenance.
Policy changes are audited and cannot silently weaken an already active event.
issues.risk: Inconsistent checks across endpoints could bypass event policy.
issues.owner_role: Backend engineer and contest policy owner

issues.title: Build an organizer workflow for contest draft, preview and publication
issues.problem: Organizers have no supported interface to prepare a validated contest.
scope: Create a proposed organizer feature with draft editing, problem ordering, timing and assistance-policy preview.
Require explicit publication confirmation showing the final immutable rules and validation errors.
acceptance: A participant cannot access organizer mutations even by calling their API directly.
A draft with missing problem versions or invalid times cannot publish.
A complete original-problem event can be prepared, previewed and published in an end-to-end test.
issues.risk: Administrative forms can expose mutation permissions or conceal critical rules.

issues.title: Implement audited contest rejudging with immutable verdict revisions
issues.problem: Organizers need to correct grading errors without overwriting the evidence behind earlier standings.
scope: Add proposed authorized rejudge requests with reason, selected grading version and append-only result revision.
Recompute affected standings from the chosen official revision while retaining prior visible audit history.
acceptance: Repeated identical rejudge requests enqueue no duplicate active job.
Unapproved/failed rejudges leave official standings unchanged.
A completed approved rejudge changes the expected score and records actor, reason and prior revision reference.
issues.risk: A faulty correction can retroactively invalidate many results.

issues.title: Add contest clarification and appeal records with controlled disclosure
issues.problem: Participants need a traceable correction channel that does not reveal another team’s private work.
scope: Add proposed private participant questions, organizer responses and separately approved public clarifications.
Link a grading appeal to an attempt/rejudge decision with bounded text and a visible state history.
acceptance: A private clarification is visible only to its participant/team and authorized organizers.
Publishing a clarification requires explicit organizer action and does not auto-copy private source.
Appeal resolution links to the official result revision without modifying the original report.
issues.risk: Support discussions can leak hidden cases or identifiable submissions.

issues.title: Deliver bounded scoreboard polling with consistent event revisions
issues.problem: A leaderboard must refresh reliably without exposing frozen results or creating an unbounded request loop.
scope: Add a proposed scoreboard view using bounded polling, conditional/versioned responses and explicit stale/error states.
Render ties, team names and freeze state from server projections; cancel requests on navigation.
acceptance: A response from an older event revision cannot overwrite a newer display.
Polling stops on navigation and backs off after failures under fake-clock tests.
Narrow-screen and keyboard flows expose the same frozen/public data as the API.
issues.risk: Out-of-order updates and aggressive polling can harm fairness or availability.

issues.title: Create a reproducible contest rehearsal and official standings export
issues.problem: A contest feature set needs an end-to-end operational gate rather than separate passing screens.
scope: Add a proposed deterministic rehearsal using only original fixtures: register, submit AC/WA, freeze, clarify, rejudge and finish.
Export versioned official standings with event/rules identifiers and exclude private source and grading inputs.
acceptance: The exported standings match a hand-checked expected fixture and replay to identical ordering.
The rehearsal covers an unauthorized participant, pending job at deadline and a failed rejudge.
Each export records its event revision; no real learner database is modified by the rehearsal.
issues.risk: An incomplete rehearsal can hide event-wide correctness failures.

issues.title: Version output-comparison policies without changing existing verdicts
issues.problem: Existing grading needs an explicit comparison-policy boundary before supporting richer problem types.
scope: Add a proposed trusted comparison-policy registry with exact and documented whitespace/token policies.
Bind a policy version to a problem/grading version and retain current seed-problem semantics.
acceptance: Current seed solutions keep their previous verdicts.
Fixtures distinguish trailing newline, extra tokens, encoding errors and output-size bounds.
Unknown comparator IDs fail closed rather than selecting a permissive default.
out_of_scope: Running arbitrary checker scripts on the host
issues.risk: A permissive comparator can accept incorrect programs.

issues.title: Add isolated versioned custom-checker support for authorized problems
issues.problem: Some original problems need custom validation, but checker code cannot gain host execution privileges.
scope: Design a proposed bounded checker protocol and execute approved checker artifacts through the isolated runtime.
Separate checker/runtime failure from learner wrong answer and limit feedback to permitted summaries.
acceptance: A valid alternative output is accepted and an invalid witness is rejected by maintained fixtures.
Checker timeout, malformed result and attempted network/host-file access fail closed with cleanup.
Private expected data and checker diagnostics never appear in participant responses.
out_of_scope: Production approval of an unaudited execution engine
issues.risk: Checker privileges and diagnostic leakage expand the execution trust boundary.

issues.title: Implement bounded floating-point answer validation
issues.problem: Numerical problems require explicit tolerance semantics rather than ad hoc string conversion.
scope: Add a proposed versioned comparator with approved absolute/relative tolerance and token-count rules.
Reject malformed numbers, non-finite values and unsupported locale formats deterministically.
acceptance: Boundary fixtures cover both tolerance limits, signed zero, scientific notation and extreme finite magnitudes.
NaN/infinity/extra-token outputs cannot bypass validation.
Problem metadata cannot choose unbounded or negative tolerances.
issues.risk: Floating-point edge cases can produce false acceptance or rejection.

issues.title: Introduce explicit subtask scoring for separately configured events
issues.problem: Future partial-score tasks need a contract that does not silently reinterpret ICPC AC/WA scoring.
scope: Add a proposed problem-version subtask/weight contract with bounded aggregate score reporting.
Keep partial-score events distinct from ICPC scoring and withhold private case details.
acceptance: Weights and dependencies validate before a task is released.
Hand-calculated pass/fail fixtures yield exact deterministic subtask totals.
ICPC and ordinary practice results remain byte-compatible in their existing public fields.
out_of_scope: Changing every existing contest to IOI rules
issues.risk: Mixing score models can silently change rankings.
issues.owner_role: Judge engineer and contest product owner

issues.title: Add an audited C++20 runtime alongside existing C++17
issues.problem: C++20 is a roadmap language, but the current supported contract is C++17.
scope: Add a proposed explicit C++20 language ID/compiler mode while retaining C++17.
Advertise the runtime only after compiler/version and isolation probes succeed; update editor/submission validation together.
acceptance: A C++20-only original fixture compiles and passes while the existing C++17 suite remains green.
Compiler errors, time/output limits and cleanup execute through the same isolation boundary.
A missing compiler mode does not appear as an available language.
out_of_scope: Claiming all C++20 library features across compilers
Upgrading the managed host runtime without approval
issues.risk: Compiler-mode drift can make editor and judge capabilities disagree.

issues.title: Add isolated Java support with explicit JVM resource semantics
issues.problem: Java support requires JVM-aware startup and limits, not only a language dropdown.
scope: Add a proposed pinned JDK toolchain, class/main contract and versioned compilation/run command.
Document runtime overhead and supported resource accounting before enabling the capability.
acceptance: Original fixtures cover successful execution, compilation failure, uncaught exception and deadline/output limits.
JVM startup overhead is included in the documented total deadline; host process execution is never used.
Capability remains unavailable if preflight or resource enforcement fails.
out_of_scope: Claiming aggregate memory measurement without runtime support
issues.risk: JVM memory reservations can conflict with existing per-process limits.

issues.title: Add isolated JavaScript support with denied network and bounded runtime
issues.problem: JavaScript submissions need an independent untrusted-code runtime, not the application Node process.
scope: Add a proposed pinned sandbox Node runtime and a documented stdin/stdout/module contract.
Disable package installation and retain sandbox network, process, filesystem and output restrictions.
acceptance: Original success, syntax-error, rejected-network, process-spawn and infinite-loop fixtures produce documented results.
Learner code cannot read application state or inherit provider/worker credentials.
The browser and API reject JavaScript submissions when its preflight is not ready.
issues.risk: Reusing the application runtime would collapse the isolation boundary.

issues.title: Add isolated Go compilation with offline standard-library execution
issues.problem: Go is feasible only with a reproducible offline compiler and bounded compilation/runtime behavior.
scope: Add a proposed pinned Go toolchain and standard-library-only submission contract.
Set deterministic compilation environment and forbid module downloads inside jobs.
acceptance: Success, compile-error, excessive goroutine/output and timeout fixtures remain bounded and cleaned up.
An attempted remote module import cannot cause outbound fetch.
Existing Python/C++ grading remains unchanged and capabilities reflect actual Go readiness.
issues.risk: Compiler caches, network resolution and concurrent goroutines need bounded policy.

issues.title: Add isolated Rust compilation with a fixed edition and no dependency fetch
issues.problem: Rust submissions require a toolchain/edition contract and compile budgets separate from application builds.
scope: Add a proposed pinned rustc toolchain and standard-library-only edition contract.
Bound compilation and program execution independently; reject Cargo dependency retrieval.
acceptance: Original success, borrow/type-error, panic, output-limit and compile-timeout fixtures produce documented results.
No job downloads crates or modifies a shared writable compiler cache.
Unavailable toolchain/preflight prevents advertising Rust support.
issues.risk: Long compilation or shared cache mutation can exhaust capacity or contaminate jobs.

issues.title: Enforce institutional sponsorship and learner data-use boundaries
issues.problem: An institutional pilot needs explicit limits on what an organization controls versus the learner’s personal account.
scope: Add a proposed institution/cohort sponsorship policy record with accepted terms version and permitted data scopes.
Ensure institutional administrators can manage sponsored assignments without inheriting personal practice/source access.
acceptance: An institutional administrator is denied unrelated personal history and source detail routes.
Terms/scope changes require the documented acknowledgement path and an audit record.
Pilot enrollment fails clearly when the organization’s required policy configuration is missing.
out_of_scope: Redesigning the foundational account deletion/retention system
issues.risk: Institutional roles can unintentionally override personal privacy.

issues.title: Export institution-authorized assignment records with redaction tests
issues.problem: Institutions need a narrow portable assignment record without receiving unrelated private learner data.
scope: Add a proposed versioned export for authorized cohorts/assignments and an explicit field allowlist.
Default to summary/rubric records; include source only when the assignment consent/policy explicitly permits it.
acceptance: A seeded mixed personal/cohort history exports only the requested institution’s allowed assignment rows.
Private grading data, tokens, account keys and unrelated identifiers never appear.
Expired/revoked institution permissions cannot generate or retrieve a fresh export.
issues.risk: Portable exports can turn a narrow permission mistake into a durable data leak.

issues.title: Produce a redacted pilot cost ledger and resource-envelope report
issues.problem: A sustainable pilot needs measured usage and declared prices rather than assumptions that self-hosting or AI is free.
scope: Add a proposed offline report combining bounded usage aggregates with operator-supplied nonsecret unit prices.
Separate measured consumption, estimated allocation and unpriced items; never infer a paid purchase from report generation.
Consume B021/B053 measurements and the B003 approved envelope; never create another online token/budget reservation ledger.
acceptance: Known usage/price fixtures produce exact totals and missing prices remain explicitly unknown.
The report excludes source, personal identifiers and provider credentials.
A budget scenario exceeding its approved resource envelope is flagged with the contributing categories.
out_of_scope: Live invoicing, payment processing or guaranteed profitability
issues.risk: False precision can hide unpriced support, capacity or provider costs.

issues.title: Extend existing pilot grants with expiring institutional scopes
issues.problem: A limited pilot needs enforceable access grants and a recorded go/no-go decision before any commercial expansion.
scope: Extend B049 admission authority with owner-approved institutional scope, expiry and revocation; do not add a parallel entitlement or budget ledger.
Use B117 sponsorship/data-use boundaries and B119 resource reports to decide an explicitly approved pilot envelope.
Make revocation stop new admission while documenting bounded treatment of in-flight authorized jobs.
Reuse B050/B051 reservations and spend limits for institutional grants; no parallel accounting store.
acceptance: Expired/revoked grants cannot access the gated workflow; existing ordinary practice remains available.
A grant cannot override contest assistance rules, ownership boundaries or hard execution/model budgets.
The release record lists the tested revision, approved audience/capacity, unresolved risks and accountable owner.
out_of_scope: Automatic charging or creating paid subscriptions
Declaring public production readiness from the existence of a grant
issues.risk: A commercial access flag must not become a bypass for safety or privacy policy.

issues.title: Separate evaluation splits and report archive contamination candidates
issues.problem: Archived benchmark variants contain overlapping tasks, and public model training history is incomplete. Reusing them naively can contaminate training/evaluation comparisons.
scope: Define immutable split manifests by problem/source/date lineage rather than file name alone.
Compute permitted exact/normalized overlap fingerprints and flag near-duplicate candidates for review.
Record unknown model-training exposure as uncertainty rather than claiming a clean benchmark.
acceptance: The same task cannot enter training and evaluation splits under different variant filenames.
Every exclusion/override records its reason and owner.
Original archives stay byte-identical; analysis outputs contain hashes/metadata rather than copied benchmark bodies.
validation: Future authorized check: deterministic synthetic overlap fixtures; static manifest review before any real-data analysis.
out_of_scope: Claiming zero contamination for closed models
issues.risk: Approximate deduplication needs human review and cannot establish unseen model pretraining data.

issues.title: Register dataset and model permissions separately from source licenses
issues.problem: MIT/Apache source notices do not authorize benchmark redistribution, training, commercial use or model-weight deployment; five archived datasets are only pointers.
scope: Define machine-readable provenance with source, owner, version/hash, permitted uses, evidence and unresolved status.
Require separate flags for evaluate/train/redistribute/commercial/model-serving permissions.
Represent missing LFS objects explicitly and block activation until content and rights are available.
acceptance: Unknown or absent permission never defaults to allowed.
A source-code license cannot satisfy an unrelated dataset/model permission field.
Each approved experiment references complete immutable inputs and review evidence.
validation: Future authorized check: schema fixtures using synthetic rights records; owner review of actual permission evidence without bulk downloads.
out_of_scope: Fetching all missing LFS datasets automatically
issues.risk: Permission metadata can be incomplete or expire; record review date and responsible owner.

issues.title: Produce a resource-and-integrity feasibility decision for one self-hosted model
issues.problem: Archived ranker/solver code permits remote model code and names consumer-hardware models, but current hardware, artifact integrity, licensing and serving economics are unverified.
scope: Compare one pinned checkpoint/quantization against the approved provider baseline using documented memory, concurrency and maintenance requirements.
Review model code/license/artifact hashes and reject arbitrary trust_remote_code loading as a default.
Specify the separate approval, isolated environment and fixed budget needed for an empirical serving experiment.
acceptance: Decision names an exact artifact/revision and states unknown measurements honestly.
No weight download, remote-code execution or GPU purchase occurs during the feasibility issue.
Recommendation includes a measurable evaluation plan and a do-not-proceed outcome when resources are inadequate.
validation: Static artifact/terms/hardware review and comparison table; optional empirical commands remain unexecuted until separately approved.
issues.risk: Published memory or benchmark claims may not hold under this project's concurrency and isolation requirements.

issues.title: Add an explicit admission gate for reproducible fine-tuning experiments
issues.problem: The archived trainer can start expensive, nondeterministic work, while Solver AI has no proven baseline, approved complete dataset or production training workflow.
scope: Define and validate an experiment manifest covering rights-approved disjoint data, base artifact, seed, hyperparameters, external compute, spend ceiling and owner approval.
Require a matched untuned baseline and an evaluation/negative-result publication plan.
Reject manifests that request training inside the application workspace or omit rollback/artifact-retention rules.
acceptance: Missing approval, dataset/model permission, budget or disjoint evaluation split prevents experiment admission.
Manifest validation performs no training, cloud provisioning or model loading.
Promotion criteria compare quality, cost and regressions; failure to improve is a valid recorded outcome.
validation: Future authorized check: synthetic manifest validation fixtures and owner review; any actual training is a separate approved execution task.
out_of_scope: Promising that tuning improves solver correctness
issues.risk: Training can memorize evaluation tasks or consume substantial resources without improving product value.
issues.owner_role: ML evaluation lead with project owner
